newsitem.title: USA: Ohio lawmakers unveil $5 bln school funding plan.
newsitem.headline: Ohio lawmakers unveil $5 bln school funding plan.

text.p: A group of Republican lawmakers in the Ohio House unveiled a plan Tuesday to raise about $5 billion over five years mainly for school infrastructure projects.
The plan called for a referendum on a five-year, one percent sales tax increase that would raise an average of $1 billion a year.

Revenues from the tax increase, which would become effective Jan. 1, 1998, would be distributed to schools, with $3.75 billion slated for infrastructure assistance, $1 billion for technology improvements and $250 million for instructional materials, according to a fact sheet on the plan.
It was not clear if tax revenues would be leveraged in bond issues or used as cash for the program.
Key legislative sponsors of the plan could not be reached for comment.

Schools would be required to raise matching funds in order to receive the state revenues. The percentage of those matching funds would range from five percent to 50 percent depending on the financial condition of the school district.
The lawmakers estimated the local match for the infrastructure program to total nearly $1.3 billion.
